<ANSWER>3</ANSWER>

The given statements define a large directed acyclic graph of ancestry relations (where an edge \(X \to Y\) indicates "\(X\) is an ancestor of \(Y\)").  

Tracing the unique ancestral path upward from Sharon yields the chain segment  
Linda \(\to\) Teresa \(\to \ldots \to\) Diana \(\to \ldots \to\) Mark \(\to \ldots \to\) Joseph \(\to\) Sharon.  

The same vertex Linda also lies on an ancestral path to Cynthia:  
Linda \(\to\) Teresa \(\to\) Julia \(\to \ldots \to\) Nancy \(\to \ldots \to\) Ashley \(\to \ldots \to\) Marilyn \(\to \ldots \to\) Gloria \(\to\) Cynthia.  

Thus Linda is a common ancestor of both Sharon and Cynthia (hence many other vertices farther up the same connected component are likewise common ancestors).  

No directed path exists from Sharon to Cynthia or from Cynthia to Sharon, so neither is an ancestor of the other. No common descendant of the two vertices appears among the supplied statements, and the statements supply no outgoing edges from either Sharon or Cynthia.  

Consequently the only correct statement among the five options is that Sharon and Cynthia share a common ancestor.
